title: Outflare
description: Requests, job queue, Postgres and process health for an Outflare server. See docs/monitoring.md in outflareai/outflare.

panels.title: Requests refused by rate limits
panels.description: 429s by limit: api (per token), register, site_ip (unknown site keys), site_key (per key), site_visitor (per visitor behind a site's proxy).

panels.title: Jobs due, by kind
panels.description: Jobs whose run_at has passed, waiting for a worker.

panels.title: Wait before a worker picks a job up (p95)
Jobs put back after their lease ran out
panels.description: Running jobs requeued because their worker stopped holding them (a crash, or a job longer than the lease). Each may run twice.

panels.title: Time waiting for a connection
panels.description: Above zero means the pool is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Below 99% means the working set no longer fits in memory.

panels.title: Sequential scans on large tables
panels.description: A large table scanned often is missing an index.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores in use.

panels.title: Oldest due item, by stage (the bottleneck)
panels.description: How long the longest-waiting item of each stage has waited for a worker. The highest line is the bottleneck: give that stage more workers, or find what it waits on below.

panels.title: Items due, by stage
panels.description: Items ready and waiting for a worker. A line that keeps growing is a stage that can't keep up.

panels.title: Items finished, by outcome
panels.description: What stages decided per second, across every worker.

panels.title: Why items stop
panels.description: Error and reason codes per second, by stage: rate limits, provider errors, AI failures, budget pauses, skips.

panels.title: Batch time (p95), by stage
panels.description: How long one batch takes. A slow stage with a small backlog is fine; a slow stage with a growing backlog needs more workers or a faster provider.

panels.title: Wait before a worker picks an item up (p95)
panels.description: Time from an item being due to being claimed, by stage.

panels.title: Calls held back by limits
panels.description: Calls to outside accounts that waited: rate is a rate limit, breaker is an account paused after repeated failures, probe is waiting for the one test call.

panels.title: Outside accounts: call outcomes and open breakers
panels.description: Calls by outcome per second, and accounts whose breaker is open now.

panels.title: Runs, by state
panels.description: Runs running or paused. Many paused runs usually means workspaces hit a budget or lost a connection.

panels.title: Items in progress and held
panels.description: Items claimed by workers, and items waiting for a person.

panels.title: AI calls by tool
panels.description: AI model calls booked per minute, by tool. Every call runs on the workspace's own key.

panels.title: AI spend by tool (US$ per hour)
panels.description: What AI calls cost on workspaces' own provider bills, by tool. Outflare pays for none of it.

panels.title: AI tokens by provider
panels.description: Tokens per minute, by provider and kind.

panels.title: AI limits warned and reached
panels.description: Workspaces told their AI spend reached 80% (level 80) or all (level 100) of a limit, per hour.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by outcome
panels.description: Deliveries connectors (such as Geonode) sent to /v1/hooks per minute. Normal is mostly accepted with a few duplicates; bad_signature or not_found in bulk means a wrong secret, an old address, or someone probing.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by connector
panels.description: Deliveries per minute by connector. A connector that drops to zero while it usually sends may have lost its subscription.

panels.title: Webhook events finished, by result
panels.description: Events workers finished per minute: handled, ignored (logged, nothing uses it yet), failed (gave up) and retry. Normal is no failed.

panels.title: Time from arrival to handled (p95)
panels.description: How long an event waits from arriving to a worker finishing it, by connector. Normal is a few seconds; minutes means workers are behind (see the Jobs row, kind hooks.handle).

panels.title: Domain Connect lookups by outcome
panels.description: Lookups per minute when a DNS card opens: available means the person can approve the records at their DNS provider. no_provider and not_onboarded are normal (the card falls back to a Cloudflare token); lookup_failed should stay near zero.

panels.title: Domain Connect lookup time (p95)
panels.description: How long a lookup takes, DNS and the provider's API included. Usually well under a second; cached answers are instant.

panels.title: Queries by outcome
panels.description: Queries run per minute, by outcome: invalid is SQL the database refused, timeout ran over 15 seconds, unavailable means the query role couldn't be set up.

panels.title: Query time
panels.description: How long queries take, at the median and the 95th percentile. Each runs on its own connection, at most 8 at once per server.

panels.title: Usage limits warned and reached
panels.description: Workspaces warned that a paid connection (SEO data, lead data, email verification, page reads) used 80% of a daily or monthly usage limit, or reached it, per hour. Normal: a few a day; a burst means a feature is using far more than usual.

panels.title: Calls stopped at a usage limit
panels.description: Paid connector calls Outflare did not make because the connection reached its limit, per hour, by connector. Normal: zero or a trickle; a steady stream means a feature keeps retrying into a limit and should back off.

panels.title: Items embedded
panels.description: Records, replies, meetings and deals turned into vectors per minute, with the workspace's own AI key. Bursts when a workspace first connects an AI model, then a trickle as things change.

panels.title: Embedding jobs by outcome
panels.description: Embedding jobs per minute: failed means a workspace's provider refused or failed (a bad key, its AI limit reached), and the job tries again on the next tick. A few are normal; a steady stream is not.

panels.title: pgvector and workspaces
panels.description: available is 1 when the database has pgvector; workspaces is how many have meaning-based search on with an AI model that makes embeddings. Without pgvector, search by words works and meaning-based search stays off.

panels.title: Smart list freshness
panels.description: How long since the least recently refreshed smart list was brought up to date. Lists refresh every 15 minutes, so normal is under 20 minutes; failing is lists whose last refresh failed.

panels.title: Smart list refreshes
panels.description: Refreshes per minute by outcome, and how long one takes at the 95th percentile. A refresh is one statement over a workspace's people, stopped after two minutes.

panels.title: Rule outcomes
panels.description: Rules evaluated per minute, by trigger kind and outcome: fired, or why not (no_match is normal; duplicate means a replay was caught; late and before_live are backfills that set nothing off). Absence clocks show as started and stopped.

panels.title: Rule jobs
panels.description: Rule jobs per minute by kind and outcome, and how long the slowest wait for a worker (p95). Normal is a few seconds' wait and no dead jobs.

panels.title: Absence timers
panels.description: Absence timers of active rules that ran out and wait to be handled, and how long the oldest has waited. They are handled every minute, so normal is near 0 and under two minutes.

panels.title: Active rules
panels.description: Active rules in every workspace, by trigger kind.

panels.title: Conversions sent back, by outcome
panels.description: Conversions per minute sent to ad platforms, by platform and outcome. Mostly sent is normal; skipped means no consent or nothing to match on, failed means the platform refused them.

panels.title: Oldest conversion waiting
panels.description: How long the oldest queued conversion has waited. Normal is under five minutes: the sender runs every two.

panels.title: Flag requests, by surface and outcome
panels.description: Requests per minute to decide a visitor's flags: site is the website script (one per page view on sites that use flags), api is servers. Mostly ok is normal; refused is a bad key, origin or body, error is a failure to read flags.

panels.title: Flag request time (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile time to decide a visitor's flags. Normal is a few milliseconds, since flags are kept in memory; it adds to the time before a page shows its variant.

panels.title: Flags read from memory
panels.description: Share of flag lookups answered from memory rather than Postgres. Each workspace's flags are read at most every 10 seconds per process, so on a busy site this is close to 100%.

panels.title: A/B test results time (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile time to count an A/B test's results from product events, every goal included (opening a running test's results, or ending it). Normal is under a second for most sites; it grows with a site's traffic, since each look scans the test's events.

panels.title: A/B test results counted, by outcome
panels.description: How often A/B test results are counted (ok) or fail (error, usually the 30-second limit on a big site or the database). Normal is a few a minute when people are looking, and no errors.

panels.title: Consent banner requests, by endpoint and outcome
panels.description: Requests per minute from websites' consent banners: config is the script asking for the banner's settings (on a visitor's first page, then every few minutes), choice is a visitor's choice being kept. Mostly ok is normal; refused is a bad key, origin or body, error is a failure to read or write Postgres.

panels.title: Consent banner request time (p95)
panels.description: How long the consent endpoints take at the 95th percentile. Normal is well under 100 ms; the banner waits for config on a visitor's first page.

panels.title: Consent choices, by action and region
panels.description: Visitors' choices kept per minute: accept_all, reject_all, custom (per category), opt_out (US 'Do not sell or share'), gpc and api (the site's own code). A sudden drop to zero while page views go on means the banner stopped showing or sending.

panels.title: Cookie scans, by outcome
panels.description: Scans of websites for their cookie policy, per hour: ok read at least one page; failed read none (the site was down or blocked OutflareBot). Sites with the consent banner on are scanned weekly, so a few an hour is normal.

panels.title: Cookie reports from browsers, by outcome
panels.description: Reports per minute of a site's cookie and script names from visitors' browsers (at most one a day per browser). Mostly ok is normal; refused is a bad key or origin, error a failure to write to Postgres.

panels.title: Cookies and scripts new to a site
panels.description: Things found on a site for the first time, per hour: known ones go straight into its cookie policy, unknown ones wait for a person to classify them. A steady stream of unknown ones means the vendor catalogue is missing something common.

panels.title: Review page reads by outcome
panels.description: Reads of brands' review pages through each workspace's own page reader, by platform and outcome. Normal: mostly success. A failed read is retried in a browser at once, then the same day after 15 minutes, 1 and 2 hours, then every 4 hours. blocked: the site showed a bot check; page_not_found: a wrong address; not_a_review_page: the site answered but the parser found nothing (it may have changed its page); save_failed: a bug; connector_error: the page reader failed.

panels.title: New reviews kept
panels.description: Reviews kept for the first time, by platform. A page's first read brings its history, so spikes after a page is added are normal.

panels.title: Review pages being read
panels.description: Active review pages by platform, and how many failed their last read. Normal: few failing.

panels.title: Longest since a review page was read
panels.description: Time since the least recently read active page was read, by platform. Pages are read once a day, so normal is under 25 hours.

panels.title: Review pages stuck failing
panels.description: Active review pages whose last 3 or more reads failed, same-day retries in a browser included, by platform and error code. Normal: none. blocked means the site shows a bot check even in a browser, not_a_review_page that the site changed its page, save_failed a bug; page_not_found and connector_* are the workspace's to fix and show on its Reviews page.

panels.title: Social account reads by outcome
panels.description: Reads of social accounts' followers (X and LinkedIn connections, and public profiles through each workspace's own page reader), by channel and outcome. Normal: mostly success. A failed read is tried again the same day after 15 minutes, 1 and 2 hours, then every 4 hours. blocked: a bot check; no_follower_count: the page showed no count (private, suspended, or the site changed); page_not_found or invalid_address: a wrong link; save_failed: a bug; connector_error: the connection failed.

panels.title: Social accounts stuck failing
panels.description: Active social accounts whose last 3 or more reads failed, same-day retries included, by channel and error code. Normal: none. blocked, no_follower_count and save_failed are Outflare's to fix (they alert); the others are the workspace's and show on its Social page.

panels.title: Scheduled syncs (analytics, Search Console, ads, SEO)
Sync runs by outcome
panels.description: Scheduled sync runs of connections, by module and outcome. Normal: mostly success. A failed run is tried again soon (15 minutes, then 1, 2 and every 4 hours) instead of after its whole interval. internal: Outflare's own bug; connector_auth or connector_quota: the workspace's key or plan; connector_unavailable: the provider failed; budget_reached: an SEO budget doing its job.

panels.title: Syncs stuck failing
panels.description: Syncs of connected connections whose last 3 or more runs failed, retries included, by module and error code. Normal: none, or a few connector_auth (a workspace's expired key). internal, connector_unavailable and unknown alert.

panels.title: Posts by outcome
panels.description: Posts the publish job tried per hour, by channel and outcome. Normal is all published; failed means the channel refused a post or did not answer (each one is listed with its reason under Social); retried is a rate limit before anything was posted.

panels.title: Most overdue approved post
panels.description: How long past its time the most overdue approved post is, by channel. Posts go out within a minute or two of their time, so normal is near zero.

panels.title: Approved posts waiting
panels.description: Approved posts not out yet, by channel and state: later is scheduled ahead (normal), due is waiting for the publish job and should stay near zero.

panels.title: Link building (who links to a page, on workspaces' own SEO connections)
Link reads by reason and outcome
panels.description: Reads of who links to a page or domain, per hour: requested by people, agents and playbooks, or the weekly read of competitors' dead pages (dead_page). Normal: mostly success, in a burst after the weekly SEO snapshot. budget_reached means a connection's budget or the workspace's weekly share ran out; provider_error or connector_auth rising means Ahrefs or DataForSEO is failing or a key was revoked.

panels.title: Link prospect page checks by status
panels.description: OutflareBot's checks of link prospects' pages, per hour, by what it found. Normal: mostly up, some gone, blocked or unreachable (other people's sites). failed rising means checks are breaking: look for link_prospect.check_failed in the log.

panels.title: Internet Archive lookups by outcome
panels.description: Lookups of broken links in the Internet Archive, per hour. Normal: found and none; error rising means archive.org is slow or down, and checks go on without snapshots.

panels.title: Link pitch openers written, by outcome
panels.description: Openers the workspaces' own AI wrote for link pitches, per hour. Normal: mostly written; no_ai and ai_unavailable are workspaces without AI connected or over their limit. ai_failed rising means the model's answers broke: check link_pitches.write jobs.

panels.title: Link pitch replies read, by kind
panels.description: Replies to link pitches the workspaces' AI read, per hour, by what they say. Normal: a mix of other, declined and agreed, with few wants_payment. ai_failed rising means reading broke: check link_pitches.read_reply jobs.

panels.title: Agreed and live link checks, by outcome
panels.description: Checks of links sites agreed to add, and of live ones, per hour. Normal: mostly not_yet and still_live, some live; removed is a site taking a link down. unreachable high for hours means OutflareBot can't reach pages: check link_live.schedule_failed in the log.

panels.title: Web searches, by outcome
panels.description: Searches on workspaces' own DataForSEO or Geonode (search-results, used by link building playbooks), per hour. Normal: mostly done, some budget_reached. connector_unavailable or connector_invalid rising means the provider's search API is failing or changed: check web_search.done and api.called for readSearchResults by error code.

panels.title: News watch (saved news searches, on workspaces' own web search connections)
News search runs by outcome
panels.description: Runs of saved news searches through each workspace's own web search connection, by purpose and outcome. Normal: mostly success; connector_needed means a workspace has searches but no web search connection, usage_limit_reached that its connection hit a limit, connector_error that the provider failed.

panels.title: News searches and what they find
panels.description: Active news searches by state (failing: the last run failed), and the articles and coverage items runs keep for the first time per hour. Normal: few failing searches; finds rise and fall with the news.

panels.title: Most overdue news search
panels.description: How long past its time the most overdue active news search is. Searches are queued every minute, so this stays near 0; it climbing means the scheduler or the news.run jobs are stuck.

panels.title: News article reads
panels.description: OutflareBot's reads of new news articles for their byline, by status, and how many found a new journalist. Normal: mostly up; blocked and opted_out are sites saying no, unreachable and failed are worth a look when they climb.

panels.title: Partner conversions, by outcome
panels.description: Sign-ups, sales, refunds and custom conversions per minute reported by workspaces' backends (api) and postback URLs, by type and outcome. not_credited is normal (most customers weren't referred); rejected is bad input from the sender; error is ours.

panels.title: Partner link clicks, by outcome
panels.description: Clicks per minute on partners' short links (/r/<code>). tracked is normal; inactive is a paused program or partner (the visitor still lands); not_found is an unknown code; error means the click wasn't stored.

panels.title: Reward ledger changes
panels.description: Ledger entries per minute by kind and event: created by conversions, approved when their hold ends, reversed by refunds, paid through payouts.

panels.title: Oldest reward past its hold
panels.description: How long the oldest reward that should approve on its own has waited past its hold. Normal is under two minutes: the approver runs every minute.

panels.title: Partner imports from Tolt, by outcome
panels.description: Imports of partner programs from another platform (Tolt) that finished in the last hour, by connector and outcome. Imports are rare: a few runs around a workspace's switch-over day. failed means the platform refused the key, the program wasn't found or it kept failing; the import's own page says why.

panels.title: Objects partner imports read, by kind and result
panels.description: What imports did with each object they read, per minute: created here, updated (a status brought over), unchanged (here already, normal on a second run) or skipped (listed on the import as an issue). A lot of skipped means the platform's data doesn't fit; look at the import's issues.

panels.title: Postbacks to partners' trackers, by outcome
panels.description: Calls to affiliates' own trackers per hour. sent is normal; retried and unreachable are a tracker that is down (theirs) or this server unable to reach outside addresses; rejected is a tracker that refused the URL (the partner's template).

panels.title: Meeting events recorded, by status
panels.description: Meeting events per minute recorded on people's timelines (meeting.booked, held, no_show, canceled), from calendars, CRMs, the app and the API. It follows how many meetings are booked and change; a backfill after an upgrade shows as one burst.

panels.title: Meetings waiting for their event
panels.description: Meetings tied to a person whose latest status isn't on their timeline yet. Normal is near zero, drained every minute; a backlog that stays means the meeting events loop is failing (meeting_events.run_failed in the log).
